sections.context: SPEC.md defines Plot as the coordination substrate for the os-eco multi-agent ecosystem — a typed, queryable, JSON-backed binder that holds intent and an append-only event log per unit of work, referencing (not embedding) seeds issues, agent runs, PRs, and mulch records. The V1 scope laid out in SPEC §3–10 is the minimum viable substrate warren and overstory need to shift from a run-centric to a Plot-centric topology. Nothing of substance is implemented yet (only version skeleton in src/), so V0.1.0 is the first usable release that lets a human author a Plot, attach references, transition status, and lets agents prime context + append events under enforced write-ACL.
sections.approach: Build bottom-up from the data model: types & schema first, then file IO (JSON + JSONL with locking and atomic writes per §4.4), then the SQLite index (§5), then the PlotStore library API (§10). Write-ACL (§6), schema versioning (§7), and the hardcoded `implementer` view (§8) layer on top of the library. CLI surfaces (§9) wrap the library last so all behavior is testable at the library level before any subcommand is wired. Files-on-disk stay the sole source of truth — SQLite is purely derived (§4.1, §5.4). Conventions follow the sibling primitives (mulch, seeds): Bun runtime, biome lint, tsc typecheck, atomic writes + file locking. Defer everything in SPEC §11 (design/plan sections, configurable views, multi-user, non-SQLite backends, push ingestors, status-tag triggers, cross-Plot DAGs, web UI).

alternatives.name: Single-file Plot (no JSONL split)
alternatives.rejected_because: SPEC §4.2 explicitly rejects this — the two write-frequency profiles (low-rate intent edits vs high-rate event appends) need different file formats so git merges stay tractable. Treating both as one file is `the source of pain` per the spec.

alternatives.name: Ship a non-SQLite backend (Postgres/Supabase) in V0.1.0
alternatives.rejected_because: SPEC §11 defers non-SQLite backends to V2. The PlotIndex interface ships so plug-in is possible, but only SQLite needs to land for the single-user binder to work.

alternatives.name: Build CLI-first, library-second
alternatives.rejected_because: Library is consumed directly by warren/overstory/sapling per §13. CLI-first risks coupling logic to argv parsing and forces a refactor before any consumer can embed it. Library-first lets the CLI be a thin shell.

alternatives.name: Configurable views in V0.1.0
alternatives.rejected_because: SPEC §8.3 says defer until V1 use proves what views are needed beyond `implementer`. Building a view DSL before knowing the second concrete view is premature abstraction.

steps.title: Define Plot data model: TypeScript types + JSON schema
steps.description: Implement the §3 data model as TS types and a JSON schema validator. Plot file shape (id, name, status enum, timestamps, intent {goal, non_goals[], constraints[], success_criteria[]}, attachments[]), event types (§3.2 table: plot_created, intent_edited, status_changed, attachment_added, attachment_removed, run_dispatched, decision_made, question_posed, question_answered, artifact_produced, note), ID format helpers (pl-<8 base32>, att-<3 digit>), actor regex (user:<handle> | agent:<name>[:<run-id>]). Export from src/ so downstream steps consume the same types. No file IO yet.

steps.title: File IO layer: JSON read/write, JSONL append, file locking, atomic writes
steps.description: Implement .plot/pl-xxx.json read/write (pretty-printed, sorted keys for clean git diffs per §4.2) and .plot/pl-xxx.events.jsonl append-only writes. Use file locking + atomic writes (write-temp-then-rename) to match mulch/seeds conventions (§4.4). Provide a streaming event-log reader. Handle missing-file cases (returns empty/null, not throw). No business logic — pure storage primitives that the PlotStore wraps.

steps.title: PlotIndex interface + SQLitePlotIndex implementation
steps.description: Implement the §5 interface: rebuild(plotsDir), query(PlotQuery), subscribe(plotId, onChange). Default impl SQLitePlotIndex backed by .plot/.index.db (gitignored). Indexed fields must be derivable from source files only (§5.4 invariant). rebuild() scans .plot/ and reconstructs the index from JSON + JSONL files; first read auto-rebuilds if .index.db is missing. Define PlotQuery shape covering at minimum: list plots by status, find plot by id, recent events of given types for a plot. Tests must include a rebuild-from-files round-trip.

steps.title: PlotStore library API: create/get/edit/attach/append/setStatus
steps.description: Implement the §10 surface: `new PlotStore({dir, index, actor})`, `store.create({name})`, `store.get(id)`, and on a Plot handle: `.editIntent({goal?, non_goals?, constraints?, success_criteria?})`, `.attach({type, ref, role})`, `.detach(attId)`, `.setStatus(status)`, `.append({type, data})`, `.answer(questionId, text)`. Each mutation writes both the JSON file (where applicable) and an event to the JSONL log, then notifies the index. Auto-generates pl-/att- IDs. No ACL enforcement yet — that lands next step. No view rendering yet.

steps.title: Write-ACL enforcement (§6)
steps.description: Enforce the §6 table at Plot.append(): reject `intent_edited`, `status_changed`, `attachment_removed`, `question_answered` from any actor that isn't `user:*`; reject `decision_made`, `question_posed`, `artifact_produced` from any actor that isn't `agent:*`. Actor resolution: PLOT_ACTOR env > configured `actor` > fail loudly. Error messages must point the caller at the allowed alternative (the spec calls out `question_posed` as the agent-side substitute for wanting intent changed). Tests cover every disallowed (actor, event) combination.

steps.title: Schema versioning + migrate-on-read scaffolding (§7)
steps.description: Every Plot file carries `schema_version` (V1: 1). Implement a migrations registry keyed by source version; when reading a file at version M < N, run the chain in-memory and return the upgraded shape. Write-back only happens when something else edits the Plot. For V0.1.0 there are no real migrations yet, but the scaffolding + a no-op v1→v1 case + tests for the registry must ship so V2 additions don't break branch-time-travel (§7).

steps.title: Hardcoded `implementer` view (§8.1)
steps.description: Implement `plot.view('implementer')` returning: intent (all fields), last 20 events of types {decision_made, question_posed, question_answered, artifact_produced, note}, attachments whose role ∈ {tracks, implements, informs, reference}. Use the index where it speeds things up but keep correctness derived from source files. No view DSL — a single concrete function. Tests cover empty plot, plot with >20 events (truncation), filter-by-role correctness.

steps.title: Human-facing CLI commands (§9.1)
steps.description: Wire thin CLI subcommands over the library: `plot init <name>`, `plot list`, `plot show <id>`, `plot edit <id>` (opens intent in $EDITOR), `plot intent <id> --goal --non-goal --constraint --success-criterion`, `plot status <id> <state>`, `plot attach <id> <type>:<ref> --role <role>`, `plot detach <id> <att-id>`, `plot answer <id> <question-id> "..."`. Actor defaults to `user:<git config user.email handle>` per the §12.4 lean answer. Use whatever argv parser the sibling tools (seeds/mulch) use to keep conventions consistent.

steps.title: Agent-facing CLI commands (§9.2) + env conventions
steps.description: Implement `plot get <id> --view implementer` (renders the view as JSON for agent consumption) and `plot append <id> --event <type> --data <json>`. Honor PLOT_ID env so agents can omit `<id>` (orchestrator sets it on dispatch per §9.2). Honor PLOT_ACTOR env (required for agents per §12.4). ACL errors from the library surface as non-zero exits with the corrective hint in the message.

steps.title: Operational CLI commands (§9.3): rebuild-index, sync, doctor
steps.description: `plot rebuild-index` wipes and regenerates .plot/.index.db from source files. `plot sync` stages + commits .plot/ changes (matches `sd sync` / `ml sync` ergonomics). `plot doctor` replays each event log against its JSON file, checks file integrity, and surfaces the §12.3 warning when an attachment ref can't be located in its source system. Tests cover the round-trip: corrupt the index → rebuild → identical query results.

steps.title: Integration tests, README usage examples, .gitignore wiring
steps.description: End-to-end tests that drive the CLI through a realistic flow: init → editIntent → attach (seeds_issue) → setStatus ready → append (decision_made as agent) → view implementer → rebuild index → doctor. README documents the §10 library surface and §9 CLI surface with copy-pasteable examples mirroring SPEC's JSON samples. Ensure .gitignore includes `.plot/.index.db` per §4 file layout. bun test, lint, typecheck all green.

steps.title: V0.1.0 release prep: CHANGELOG, version bump, publish dry-run
steps.description: Bump version to 0.1.0 in package.json and src/version.ts (kept in sync per §14). Populate CHANGELOG.md with the V0.1.0 surface: data model, file storage, SQLite index, write-ACL, implementer view, full CLI. Run `npm publish --dry-run` (or `bun publish --dry-run`) against @os-eco/plot-cli to confirm the published shape. Tag once the PR lands. Do NOT push the tag from this plan — leave that to the human.

risks: Concurrent JSONL appends from agents on different git branches produce ordering ambiguity on merge. SPEC §12.2 leans timestamp-then-actor lexicographic order; may need a git merge driver, which is out of scope for V0.1.0 but should be noted in CHANGELOG so warren knows.

Index drift: it's easy to accidentally store data in SQLite that isn't derivable from source files, breaking the §5.4 invariant and the 'clone the repo and you have everything' story. Tests must explicitly verify rebuild-from-files reproduces every queryable field.

ACL bypass surface area: any code path that writes to .events.jsonl outside of Plot.append() bypasses §6 enforcement. The file IO layer must be private to PlotStore; no public re-export of the raw appender.

Schema versioning scaffolding shipping without real migrations risks rotting before V2 — easy to land an incompatible v2 schema and discover the registry was never exercised. Mitigate with a synthetic 'fake v0 → v1' test fixture that exercises the chain.
CLI ergonomics drift from sibling tools (seeds, mulch). Reuse the same argv parser, same --format flags, same actor env conventions to keep agent-facing UX uniform.
Attachment validation is deferred to `plot doctor` warnings (§12.3 lean); risk is silent rot of broken refs. Acceptable for V0.1.0 but should be documented in README.
acceptance: A human can run `plot init`, edit intent, attach a seeds issue, and transition status to `ready` using only CLI commands listed in §9.1.

An agent (PLOT_ACTOR=agent:test:run-1, PLOT_ID set) can run `plot get --view implementer` and `plot append --event decision_made --data {...}` and see the event in the log — but `plot append --event intent_edited` returns a non-zero exit with a message pointing at `question_posed`.
Deleting .plot/.index.db and running `plot rebuild-index` reproduces identical query results to the prior index — verified by an integration test.
Every Plot file written carries `schema_version: 1`; the migrations registry runs (no-op) on read; an added synthetic legacy fixture migrates cleanly in-memory.

The `implementer` view returns intent + the last 20 events filtered to {decision_made, question_posed, question_answered, artifact_produced, note} + attachments whose role ∈ {tracks, implements, informs, reference}, matching §8.1 exactly.
`bun test`, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` all green; `bun publish --dry-run` succeeds against @os-eco/plot-cli at version 0.1.0; CHANGELOG.md documents the V0.1.0 surface.

sections.context: Nightwatch patrol over plot-cli on 2026-05-28. Lint, typecheck, and 261 tests pass cleanly, but a methodical read of src/cli/commands/*.ts and src/cli/commands/doctor.ts surfaced three concrete quality issues worth fixing before the next release: (1) the --json output format is inconsistent across commands (some commands emit pretty-printed JSON, others emit compact JSON); (2) one CLI error message lacks the standard `plot <command>:` prefix used by every other error path; (3) the doctor command's event replay silently coerces malformed intent_edited payloads instead of reporting them as findings. None of these require new features, dependencies, or API changes — they are pure internal alignment.
sections.behavior_invariant: Public library API signatures in src/store.ts, src/io.ts, src/views.ts, and src/types.ts remain unchanged. CLI commands keep the same set of flags, positional arguments, exit codes, and primary success paths. JSON output stays valid JSON for every command and keeps the same field names and structure — only indentation may change. Existing tests in src/cli/router.test.ts, src/store.test.ts, and src/integration.test.ts continue to pass once they are updated to match any tightened output. `bun test`, `biome check --error-on-warnings .`, and `tsc --noEmit` remain green at the end.
sections.approach: One small PR per finding. Each step lists exact files and line ranges plus the fix shape. Steps are independent and can land in any order; the final step is the release.

steps.title: Standardize --json output formatting across CLI commands
steps.description:
Inconsistency: `--json` is pretty-printed (`JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)`) in some commands and compact (`JSON.stringify(x)`) in others.

Pretty-printed today:
- src/cli/commands/append.ts:116 (default branch)
- src/cli/commands/get.ts:50 (default branch)
- src/cli/commands/intent.ts:60 (`--json`)
- src/cli/commands/list.ts:17 (`--json`)
- src/cli/commands/show.ts:20 (`--json`)

Compact today:
- src/cli/commands/answer.ts:40 (`--json`)
- src/cli/commands/attach.ts:44 (`--json`)
- src/cli/commands/detach.ts:21 (`--json`)
- src/cli/commands/doctor.ts:91 (`--json`)
- src/cli/commands/init.ts:23 (`--json`)
- src/cli/commands/rebuild-index.ts:22 (`--json`)
- src/cli/commands/status.ts:28 (`--json`)
- src/cli/commands/sync.ts:109 (`--json`)

Fix: pick one policy and apply uniformly. Recommended: emit compact JSON for `--json` / agent-default JSON across all commands (one object per line is the easiest shape for downstream JSONL pipelines and matches the jsonl convention already used for events). Update src/cli/commands/{append.ts,get.ts,intent.ts,list.ts,show.ts} to drop the `null, 2` argument. Update src/cli/router.test.ts and src/cli/format.test.ts where they assert on indented output. Do NOT change the human-readable `--pretty` paths in `get`/`append` — those remain pretty.

If the maintainers prefer the opposite policy (always pretty), apply it the other direction; the only requirement is that every `--json` callsite agrees.

steps.title: Prefix `plot status` invalid-status error with command name
Flag malformed intent_edited payloads in doctor replay instead of silent coercion
steps.description:
src/cli/commands/doctor.ts replayPlot (~lines 240-275) silently coerces malformed `intent_edited` event payloads:
  - if field === "goal" and value is not a string, it assigns `""`
  - if field is a list field and value is not an array, it falls through with no update

validateEventShape (~lines 145-195) only validates that `ev.data` is an object — it does not validate the inner field/value shape — so a `{ field: "goal", value: 5 }` event passes shape validation and then silently corrupts replay, masking real `intent_drift`.

Fix: in doctor.ts, add a per-event-type payload shape check (either inside validateEventShape or as a sibling helper called from it) that emits a `code: "invalid_event_data"` finding (severity: error) when:
  - intent_edited.data.field is not one of INTENT_FIELDS
  - intent_edited.data.field === "goal" but data.value is not a string
  - intent_edited.data.field is a list field but data.value is not an array of strings
  - attachment_added.data is missing id/type/ref/role or has non-string values
  - attachment_removed.data.id is not a string
  - status_changed.data.{from,to} is not a PlotStatus

At minimum cover the intent_edited cases since those are the ones replayPlot swallows today. Add a test in src/cli/router.test.ts (the doctor describe block) that writes a malformed intent_edited event and asserts the new finding fires.

Do NOT change replayPlot's coercion behavior itself unless trivial — flagging is the primary fix.

steps.title: Release: run /release per .claude/commands/release.md
steps.description: After the preceding fixes land, prepare a release per .claude/commands/release.md: review changes since the last tag, bump patch version via `bun run version:bump patch`, update CHANGELOG.md, README.md, and CLAUDE.md if needed, then commit as `release: vX.Y.Z`.

acceptance: bun test passes (261+ tests, all green)
Every `--json` output across CLI commands uses the same indentation policy (verified by grep over src/cli/commands/*.ts)
Every CLI error message that comes from a command handler starts with `plot <command>: ` (verified by reading src/cli/commands/*.ts)
Doctor emits an `invalid_event_data` finding (severity: error) for an `intent_edited` event whose `value` does not match its `field` type
